== Objectives ==
Speak with [[Gornek]]. You recall Kaltunk marking your map with his location and mentioning that gornek resides in the Den, a building to the west.

== Description ==
Finally, you are of age, <name>... of age to battle in the name of the Horde. To conquer for the glory of the [[Warchief]].

Yes...

<[[Kaltunk]] looks you over.>

You will do nicely.

No doubt you wish to find a great dragon or demon and strangle it with your bare hands, but perhaps it would be wise to start on something less... dangerous.

<Kaltunk laughs.>

Report to Gornek, he should be able to assign a task better suited to a young <class>. You will find Gornek in the Den, to the west.

==Rewards==
You will receive:
* 40 [[XP]]
* +50 [[reputation]] with [[Orgrimmar (faction)|Orgrimmar]]
* +50 [[reputation]] with [[Darkspear Trolls (faction)|Darkspear Trolls]]

== Completion ==
Another one of Kaltunk's recruits, hm?

A sorry state of affairs we find ourselves in if this is the best the Horde can produce. No matter. By the time we think you're ready to leave the [[Valley of Trials|Valley]], you'll be a proud warrior of the Horde.

Zaynn Ravengarde, simply known as Zaynn, was a [[Human]] Paladin and a Knight. Zaynn eventually became a paladin and a lawful mercenary. He is the owner of '''“Five Stars Apple Cider”.'''

=='''<small>Appearance and Personality</small>'''==
Zaynn is a physically imposing man in his early 40s, sporting black with visibly graying facial hair, and a bald head. He stands at an average-tall human height of 182,5 cm (6'0" ft). His skin, kissed by sun and wind, bears a light tan. His small brown eyes, sharp and watchful, resemble those of a Redridge condor. Thin, arched eyebrows frame his gaze. His head is cleanly shaved, revealing a smooth scalp. His lips are slightly pinkish and plump, and his face resembles a shield coated in leather. 

Zaynn is a man of fiery purpose and unshakable resolve, often seen with the weight of his righteous anger in his eyes. His faith in the divine is intertwined with a deep sense of personal retribution, and every act he commits, every oath he swears, is done with the belief that he is an instrument of divine wrath. His soul burns with the need to avenge wrongs, whether they be personal slights or broader injustices in the world. His motivations are often seen as inflexible—he cares not for mercy or forgiveness, only for the restoration of balance through the execution of vengeance.

In his mind, vengeance is not just a personal crusade but a divine calling. He does not hesitate to pass judgment on those he believes have erred or betrayed the sacred tenets of the Light. Even allies, if they stray too far from the path, may find themselves facing Zaynn’s wrath. To him, there are no half-measures—punishment must be swift, absolute, and irreversible. His sense of justice is a dark mirror, reflecting his belief that only through vengeance can order be restored and evil eradicated.

== '''<small>Story</small>''' ==

=== Early Life ===
[[File:Young Zaynn.jpg|left|thumb|229x229px|Young Zaynn wearing a tabard of his house]]
Sir Zaynn was born in the year 576 K.C. His father, a well-respected trader also descendant of a noble family, instilled in him the values of honor, discipline, and chivalry from a very young age. Dreaming of becoming a knight ever since his childhood, Zaynn became a squire in his early teens to a knight named Sir Cyrus. Zaynn followed him everywhere, learning the ways of swordsmanship, strategy, and duty. Under Sir Cyrus's tutelage, Zaynn earned his knighthood in his mid 20s. Although now a knight in his own right, Zaynn always considered Sir Cyrus to be his truest mentor and guide. He would soon be assigned to serve as one of his lord's royal guards. 

Some time after the Second War, Zaynn was gifted a small piece of land by his lord in recognition of his services over the years. The area was blessed with apple trees, and Zaynn made use of the blessing to produce apple cider, generating income for his household.

=== Troubling Times ===

In the year 600 K.C., the lord whom Zaynn had served for many years died. During this time, internal strife erupted due to a dispute over the legitimacy of the heir within the noble house he served. Since Zaynn supported the losing side, he was forced into exile in foreign lands, losing his title. Zaynn then traveled south and lived at Northshire Abbey for some time. It was here that he learned to wield the power of the Holy Light, becoming a Paladin in the process. With his newly gained ability, he served the people by joining a band of mercenary based in Redridge. 

=== Settling Down ===

During his time in Redridge, Zaynn frequently visited a local tavern and met a woman named [[Clair Delun]], who worked there as a barmaid. In the year 606 K.C., after six months of courtship, Zaynn and Clair became betrothed, and they were married soon after. They lived in Lakeshire, where they lived peacefully for some time, building a life together.

Zaynn continued to serve with the Redridge mercenaries, operating mostly in the Eastern Kingdoms. Most of the time, he serves as a supporting unit, capable of fighting in close-quarters combat and healing his team. At some point before the Third War, he returned to his home and successfully reclaimed his small land once given to him by his old lord. After moving back to his old home, his apple cider business resumed and is now regularly distributed to taverns. After rebuilding his land and his business, he soon joined the other paladins to fight the scourge in the northern regions. 

=== Birth of Vengeance ===
While traveling through the Lordaeron region to assist with the fight against the Scourge, Zaynn encountered a Scourge-controlled village. While he was fighting the Scourge, he came face-to-face with an undead. Upon closer inspection, Zaynn realized that the undead was none other than Jon Agamand, his former squire, who had been turned into an abomination by the Scourge. 

Jon had been a promising young squire under Zaynn’s tutelage, filled with ambition and dreams of becoming a knight, just as Zaynn had once been. Their bond had been strong, and Zaynn had always seen Jon as a brother-in-arms. The realization that Jon had fallen to the Scourge shattered Zaynn’s heart.

Zaynn was forced to battle Jon, who had no memory of their past and fought only to destroy. In the end, Zaynn had no choice but to strike down his former squire, now an undead minion of the Scourge. The loss of Jon, someone Zaynn had once mentored and cared for, filled him with a devastating mix of sorrow and rage.

This encounter changed Zaynn forever. The ideals of justice and nobility he had once followed felt hollow in the face of such unimaginable loss. His grief turned to fury, and his quest for vengeance became all-consuming. He no longer fought simply for honor or chivalry but to rid the world of the Scourge at any cost. The death of Jon was the catalyst that transformed him into '''Zaynn the Vengeful'''.

==Relationships==
===[[Clair Delun]]===
[[File:Clair Delun.jpg|left|200x200px|thumb|Clair Delun during World of Warcraft.]]
She was a barmaid from Lakeshire who became Zaynn’s spouse. After living a generally peaceful life in Lakeshire for years, she followed her husband to reclaim his land. Together, they run a their apple cider brewery for a living. Her connections and experience from working at a tavern played a pivotal role in their cider business. After the loss of Zaynn's apprentice, she is the only person who can provide solace to his soul.

'''Power Leveling'''

This is the method the power levelers have used since closed beta and I finally got one of them to give it up. It is by no means the way to go if you want to maximize your experience in the game as this method will bypass almost all the content in the game and essentially ignore many of the fun, unique aspects of WoW. This is not recommended for new players and is meant for players who already have experienced the content and just want to level up an alt to play with their level 60 friends (ie. your level 60 instance group needs a priest and there are no priests to be had). As a benchmark to how successful you are with this, download cosmos (Cosmos) and use the clock feature to measure your xp/hour. At level 50 you should be getting about 40,000+/hour. 1-20: Newbie lands, stick to the friendly zones (not contested). Just grind. The quests are a waste of time up to level 20 if you are focusing on maxing out xp per hour. 20-26: Wetlands quests and raptors/slime/orcs for grinding. Redridge mountain Lakeshire quests.

* 26-30: Duskwood quests and undead for grinding. Hillsbrad critter roamers for grinding. 
* 30-35: Did these all in a day on Daggerspines in Hillsbrad right next to Southshore along the coast. Huge spawn, very fast respawn rate, easy mobs to kill. Purgation isle (island in the very far Southwest water area of Hillsbrad) also a nice secluded place you can grind on undead.
* 36-40: Hillsbrad southshore quests. Desolace quests and kodo grinding for 36-38, then Undead Ravagers in the southeast for 38-40. Cresting exiles at the circle of outer binding in Arathi also for 37-41; extremely easy mobs with a fast respawn. Alterac ogres from 35-40 for grinding. Drywhisker kobolds in Arathi east of Hammerfall for 36-39 for grinding.
* 41-45: Hinterlands trolls, owl beasts, and wolves for grinding and quests. Badlands ogres, gnolls, and quests.
* 45-48: Tanaris quests and pirates on the eastern paninsula for grinding. Stranglethorn vale quests (only if you need rewards imo). Badlands greater elementals for grinding.
* 48-52: Felwood deadwood gnolls for grinding and quests from the sanctuary in the south. Blasted lands dreadmauls for grinding. Un'goro crater (best started at 50) for primarily quests and grinding off the plants and tar elementals. Azshara undead highbornes and thunderhead hyppogriffs for grinding.
* 52-55: Azshara blood elves for grinding. Burning steppes dreadmaul rock ogre caves firegut ogres (very low AC) for grinding. Felwood irontree woods and cave for grinding (great spot). Western plaguelands questing for argent dawn and grinding on undead throughout the various camps.
* 55-58: Eastern plaguelands quests from the sanctuary, grinding on undead at the ruined towns. Winterspring grinding at winterfall village or Lake Kel'Theril undead highbornes (my personal favorite camp). Blackrock Stronghold in Burning Steppes for grinding.
* 58-60: "The" yeti cave in Winterspring, due Southeast of Everlook (very nice place). Grosh Gok compound ogres in Deadwind pass (great spot, no one knows about it). Eastern plaguelands Fungal Vale undead grinding and argent dawn token farming. Moonowls in northeast winterspring for grinding.

The '''Wrynn''' family (also known as the '''House of Wrynn''')[[Llane Wrynn I#Royal Gallery Statue]] is the ruling line of the [[Stormwind (kingdom)|kingdom of Stormwind]], also known as the kingdom of Azeroth. They rule the kingdom from [[Stormwind Keep]], and are helped in their duties by the [[House of Nobles]]. ==Background== The kingdom of Azeroth was originally founded by the descendants of the Arathi bloodline, who had migrated south from the nation of Arathor. Traveling past the rocky mountains of Khaz Modan, their journey finally ended after many long seasons, and they settled in the northern region of the continent they would name Azeroth. In a fertile valley, they founded the kingdom of Stormwind, which quickly became a self-sufficient power in its own right.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Seven_Kingdoms The Seven Kingdoms] It had a long and prosperous history, with the king served loyally by the knights of the [[Brotherhood of the Horse]] and the clerics of the [[Holy Order of Northshire Clerics]]. During the reign of King [[Barathen Wrynn]], the island of [[Balor]] was discovered in the Great Sea to the west of the kingdom by [[Duke Balor]], who settled upon them with like-minded followers in pursuit of greater wealth. It was soon discovered that the island was rich in resources, allowing it to prosper as a self-sufficient autonomous realm that soon became a valuable merchant port. The Grahan family, renowned in the kingdom for their mercantile prestige, was sent by King Barathen to join Duke Balor in order for Stormwind to maintain a measure of influence over the bustling maritime port,[[The Founding of Balor]] and Balor would later be brought under the sovereignty of Stormwind proper after its forces relieved a siege by the pirates of [[Plunder Island]].[[The Siege of Balor]] King Barathen's reign also saw the beginnings of the orcish incursions in Azeroth, though he died in the first year of conflict and was succeeded by his son, King [[Llane Wrynn I|Llane]]. King Llane Wrynn was assassinated by the half-orc [[Garona]] at the end of the First War, succeeded by his son [[Varian Wrynn|Varian]]. The family survived the First War, but were not restored to the throne of the kingdom until after the end of the Second War. The kingdom was renamed Stormwind after the Third War. The House of Wrynn remains in control of Stormwind, although [[Anduin Wrynn|Anduin]] (who is acting king after his Varian's disappearance) rules through co-regents. ==Known members== {| class="fandom-table" style="text-align:center;" |- style="text-align:center;" ! style="text-align:left;" | Name ! == Mob XP ==

(''This information does not appear to be correct and is undergoing review. For the correct information see [[Formulas:Mob XP]] -- [[User:Greenman|Greenman]] and [[User:Gemminie|Gemminie]]'')

When you kill a mob of a certain minimum level, you get XP.  That minimum level depends on your current level.  There is a formula to calculate that minimum level: take your level, add 1, divide by 5, and round up.  If you get less than 5, erase that number and replace it with 5.  The result is how many levels below you your minimum experience-yielding mob level is.  In short,

 MML = CL - min(ceil((CL + 1)/5), 5)

'''Zmodlor''' is a minor [[demon]] who specializes in infiltration. During the events in ''[[Cycle of Hatred]]'', he recruits citizens of [[Orgrimmar]] and [[Theramore]] into the [[Burning Blade]] and uses them to raise tensions between the [[orc]]s and [[human]]s. He was banished thanks to the combined efforts of [[Aegwynn]] and [[Jaina Proudmoore]].

==History==
===Confrontation with Aegwynn=== 
On the [[world]] of [[Azeroth]], at the very start of [[Aegwynn]]'s tenure as [[Guardian of Tirisfal]], Zmodlor appeared and started a [[cult]] called the [[Burning Blade clan|Burning Blade]]. Zmodlor's cultists took over the [[school]]house of the village [[Jortas]], planning to sacrifice its children using a sword covered in oil and set alight as a ritual tool.<ref>''[[Cycle of Hatred]]'', chapter 12</ref><ref name="CoH16">''[[Cycle of Hatred]]'', chapter 16</ref> Aegwynn appeared just in time to save the children and neutralize Zmodlor, with the event being her first ever demon banishment.<ref>''[[Cycle of Hatred]]'', chapter 14</ref>

===Zmodlor's return===
During the [[Third War]], Zmodlor was among the demons summoned to [[Azeroth]]. One of many demons who survived the war,<ref>''[[Cycle of Hatred]]'', chapter 20, pg. 208: "But when the Burning Legion attacked, they recruited many demons, including ones that had been banished by the Tirisfalen. When the war ended, several stragglers managed to stay in this world even when the legion was driven back."</ref> Zmodlor sought to destroy the fragile peace between [[Orgrimmar]] and [[Theramore]].

Zmodlor recruited both orcs and humans who were prejudiced against one another into a new incarnation of the Burning Blade cult, promising each that he was only interested in helping them destroy the other. None of his minions were aware that he was also recruiting among their enemies. Among the members of Zmodlor's Burning Blade were [[Jaina Proudmoore]]'s chamberlain, [[Kristoff (human)|Kristoff]], and [[Burx]], one of [[Thrall]]'s chief warriors. Another was the human [[Margoz (human)|Margoz]], who recruited new members in the [[Demonsbane Inn]] in Theramore. When the soldier [[Strov]] followed Margoz from the inn to investigate, Zmodlor slew him. Zmodlor later cast protective wards to trap Jaina and Aegwynn in [[Bladescar]] to prevent them from interfering.

Zmodlor's plan nearly succeeded, and a battle had already broken out at [[Northwatch Hold]] before Jaina was able to discover Zmodlor's hideout atop [[Dreadmist Peak]]. Jaina and Aegwynn confronted Zmodlor and several of his [[warlock]]s, and they were able to banish him to the Twisting Nether yet again.

Aegwynn did not believe that Zmodlor was acting on his own in using the Burning Blade to inflame violence between Orgrimmar and Theramore, telling Jaina that "a plan of this complexity is far beyond him". The identity of Zmodlor's master remained a mystery.<ref>''[[Cycle of Hatred]]'', Epilogue, pg. 237</ref>

While speaking with Thrall following these events, Jaina stated that the Burning Legion would have a hard time rescuing Zmodlor a second time and that because he is a minor demon it would not be worth the effort.<ref>''[[Cycle of Hatred]]'', pg. 234</ref>\

{{Book|content=
<The Book documents the fallen one's journey from them splitting off the Moro'gai up to the present. Some pages offer interesting insights on incidents throughout that time.>
----
We have left the others behind at Shimmerstar Lake. So far they have not tried to get in contact with us again, a circumstance I very much welcome. My followers are hard at work establishing new huts and traps for the fish at the pond we have settled. It does not compare to Shimmerstar Lake, but it should provide us with plenty of food, coupled with the wild horned beasts nearby we can hunt. We need to return to normalcy quickly, or else they will lose faith in me.
----
Last night, a glistening star illuminated the sky. Shortly after, the star fell onto the coast, much like they did back on Draenor. The impact was right next to our settlement, and while I was able to save most of my followers from the impact, many of our huts and a few unfortunate ones were caught in the blast. A heavy setback, but we will recover. We must.
----
Time has passed since the star crashed down to earth. From the crater, a gigantic crystal emerged. It is not draenethyst, but a rare gift from the Twisting Nether. My followers have recovered from the impact, somewhat atleast, but now new hurdles are laid before our path. Energy from the crystal attracted scaled fiends of azure color. From the way they act, I can feel that they knew about it beforehand. Could they have had a hand in calling it towards this world?
----
The situation has become dire. Residue from the crystal seeped into our pond and fouled the fish inside. While my tribesmen still live, eating the fish caused them to convulse in great pain or even fall into a coma. The great horned beasts also migrated mostly to the west, making survival more difficult by the day. Skirmishes with the scaled fiends happen more and more with each passing day and we don't have the power to fend them off forever.

We are surrounded by enemies and our food supplies begin to run out. Was this the path I've chosen for my kin truly the right one? Shall I falter already?
----
In my dreams, I experienced a vision. In my inner turmoil, doubts and regrets plagued my mind. Should I accept my misjudgment and return to the Moro'gai? My conviction wavered. It was then that a voice called out to me. A deep and raspy voice, once to know many eons. They spoke of my ambitions, dreams, and the loss of trust in my own abilities. And that I could reclaim my lost zeal by seeking allies in the mountains to the south. I was hesitant, but what options had I been left with? My intuition tells me to put my trust in that voice, as desperate as it may be.
----
I have sought those mysterious allies: Satyrs, as they call themselves. They are horned and tall creatures, with broad hooves. Their long claws and anguished grimace caused distrust at first, but after speaking with one of their leaders, my doubts were diminished. He called himself Selenaxx, and his people were cast into the darkness as outcasts. They worship the name [[Xavius]], whose voice I apparently heard in my dream vision. According to Selenaxx, their god is a benevolent one that seeks out those in need and shunned by the world.
----
The Satyr offered their help against our adversaries. The magic that they wield is potent and would be a great asset to assure our survival. Perhaps they could even be the key to unlock the Draenethyst's true potential... Yet still, hesitation still remains. I shall contemplate on what decision to make. For now, I am relieved to see other kindred spirits in this forsaken world.
}}
